input.strategy_title: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Public-sector deals require the model serving stack to run on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules. Today KServe
components and the serving data plane link non-validated crypto libraries in
several images, and we have no compliance evidence package. Certification
involves an external accredited laboratory (historical turnaround: six to nine
months) and mandatory security review board sign-off at defined milestones —
these human and third-party gates dominate the schedule regardless of
engineering speed.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training (separate strategies)
- Common Criteria certification

## Open Questions

None on scope — but note that lab scheduling and review-board cadence are
externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort.

# KServe FIPS 140-3 image remediation and FIPS regression CI enforcement

## Description

This epic makes the KServe model serving stack's own images — its control-plane
components and its serving data plane — run correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift
clusters using validated cryptographic modules, with no non-validated crypto in
the request path. It also delivers the FIPS regression enforcement slice for
KServe's builds: a gating CI check that fails any KServe serving-stack build
reintroducing non-validated crypto usage. The epic produces the KServe portion
of the module inventory, build attestations, and test results that the
serving-stack compliance evidence package is assembled from.

## Scope

- Audit KServe's serving-stack images (control-plane components and the
  serving data plane) to inventory non-validated cryptographic library usage,
  with focus on the request path.
- Replace non-validated crypto library usage with validated cryptographic
  modules in those images.
- Verify InferenceService deployment and request serving on FIPS-enabled
  OpenShift clusters using validated crypto modules.
- Preserve existing serving behavior on non-FIPS clusters (no functional
  regression from the crypto module change).
- Add a gating CI check on KServe serving-stack builds that fails any build
  reintroducing non-validated crypto usage, and verify it fails a build that
  reintroduces such usage.
- Produce the KServe-images module inventory and FIPS test results for
  consumption by the compliance evidence package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The module inventory for all KServe serving-stack images is complete and
  shows no non-validated cryptographic library usage in the request path.
- Models deploy and serve inference requests correctly on a FIPS-enabled
  OpenShift cluster using validated crypto modules.
- Existing serving behavior on non-FIPS clusters is unchanged by the crypto
  module replacement (no functional regression).
- A gating CI check fails a KServe serving-stack build that reintroduces
  non-validated crypto usage, and passes the remediated builds.
- The KServe module inventory and FIPS test results are produced in a form
  the compliance evidence package can consume.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: KServe's share of "all serving-stack images run correctly
  on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules" — the KServe
  control-plane and serving data plane images.
- **HLR-3 (P1, bundled)**: the CI FIPS-regression gating check for KServe
  builds. Bundled with the P0 remediation because it is an enforcement
  deliverable over the same surfaces being converted — it shares the builds
  and module-inventory data with the remediation and has no independent user
  value over unconverted builds.

# Serving-stack FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package and certification submission

## Description

This epic assembles the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the model
serving stack — module inventory, build attestations, and test results — and
submits it through the security review board to the external accredited
certification laboratory. The package draws on the remediated KServe and
Platform Operator images once their FIPS remediation is complete, so this work
starts after those remediations finish.

## Scope

- Assemble the module inventory covering all serving-stack images (KServe
  control-plane, KServe serving data plane, and Platform Operator), reconciled
  against the final remediated image builds.
- Collect build attestations for the final serving-stack images.
- Compile the FIPS test results produced by the remediation work (cluster-level
  operation on FIPS-enabled OpenShift and per-image verification).
- Package the evidence and submit it through the security review board to the
  external accredited certification lab.
- Track the submission through review-board sign-off and lab acceptance into
  review.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The module inventory covers every serving-stack image in scope and is
  reconciled against the final remediated builds (no stale or
  pre-remediation entries).
- Build attestations for the final serving-stack images are included in the
  package.
- FIPS test results demonstrating correct operation on FIPS-enabled clusters
  with validated crypto modules are included in the package.
- The complete evidence package is submitted through the security review
  board to the external accredited certification lab and accepted into the
  lab's review queue.

## Risks / Notes

- The accredited lab's turnaround is historically six to nine months and the
  security review board operates on its own cadence — both are externally
  controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort; they dominate
  the schedule regardless of engineering speed. The certification grant
  itself is outside this epic's deliverable, which ends at submission and
  acceptance into review.
- Public-sector deal timing depends on the certification outcome; plan
  commitments accordingly.
- **Owning component/team is an assumption**: this epic is attributed to
  component KServe / team RHOAI Serving (the only grounded owner in
  `architecture/rhoai-3.0/kserve.md`), but its scope spans the Platform
  Operator images as well — it assembles evidence for the whole serving
  stack. The strategy provides no Impacted Teams table to resolve the
  cross-component ownership. Confirm the owning component/team for the
  cross-component evidence package with the engagement before scheduling.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: "A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build
  attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security
  review board to the external certification lab."

# Document the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites for the model serving stack

## Description

This epic authors and publishes the documentation describing the model serving
stack's FIPS 140-3 support posture and the cluster prerequisites for running
it — what is supported, on which FIPS-enabled OpenShift configurations, and
what the certification status is. The content describes what was actually
built and submitted, so it is authored after the remediation and evidence
work completes.

## Scope

- Author documentation topics covering:
  - The FIPS support posture of the model serving stack (KServe and Platform
    Operator images), including the validated-crypto-module operating mode.
  - Cluster prerequisites: FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters and any related
    installation/configuration requirements.
  - The certification status of the stack and how to interpret it (submitted
    evidence package vs. granted certification).
- Route the content through the Red Hat docs content process to publication.
- Technically review the content against the implemented remediation and the
  submitted evidence package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the FIPS support posture of the model
  serving stack and the cluster prerequisites for running it.
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented FIPS
  remediation and the submitted compliance evidence, with review findings
  resolved.
- The documentation is available through the standard docs content process.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)**: "Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster
  prerequisites." Epic priority is P0 via the docs-authoring priority
  exception (strategy priority: Critical), not via inheritance.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9013: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack

Triage: full decomposition (not below-threshold, not docs-only). The strategy
spans multiple components (KServe, Platform Operator) and multiple distinct
work streams (crypto-library remediation code changes, compliance evidence
package assembly and submission, substantive documentation authoring), so the
below-threshold escape condition for multiple distinct work streams applies.

Staff Engineer Input: absent from the strategy — no overrides to log.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E001 | KServe FIPS 140-3 image remediation and FIPS regression CI enforcement | Implementation | RHOAI Serving | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E002 | Platform Operator FIPS 140-3 image remediation and FIPS regression CI enforcement | Implementation | RHOAI Platform | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E003 | Serving-stack FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package and certification submission | Implementation | RHOAI Serving | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E004 | Document the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites for the model serving stack | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Serving | P0 |

Note on E004 priority: HLR-4 is P2 in the strategy, but `docs-authoring` epics
derive priority from the strategy frontmatter (`priority: Critical` → P0) per
the docs-authoring priority exception; docs edges do not push priority
upstream (the P0 priorities of E001–E003 come from HLR-1/HLR-2).

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["E001 KServe FIPS image remediation + CI"] --> E003["E003 Compliance evidence package + submission"]
    E002["E002 Platform Operator FIPS image remediation + CI"] --> E003
    E001 --> E004["E004 FIPS posture documentation"]
    E002 --> E004
    E003 --> E004
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E003 | Rule 13 (artifact consumption) | The evidence package is assembled from the module inventory, build attestations, and test results of the final remediated KServe images; attesting pre-remediation images would produce invalid evidence, so the evidence epic consumes the remediation epics' outputs and is serial after them. |
| E002 → E003 | Rule 13 (artifact consumption) | Same rationale for the Platform Operator image(s): its final builds' attestations and test results are inputs to the evidence package. |
| E001 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Documentation states the FIPS support posture that the remediation establishes; blocked by every Implementation epic in the strategy. |
| E002 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Same — Platform Operator remediation is part of the posture being documented. |
| E003 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs last) | The documented posture must reflect the submitted evidence package, not a plan. |
| No edge E001 ↔ E002 | Rule 14 (parallel) | Different components and repositories with no shared artifacts; the two remediations proceed in parallel. |
| No standalone CI-enforcement epic | Step 5 shared-surface rule | HLR-3's gating FIPS-regression CI check is an enforcement deliverable that applies across the same surfaces being converted (the serving-stack images). It is divided per surface: each remediation epic delivers and verifies the regression check for its own component's builds (E001 for KServe builds, E002 for Platform Operator builds). A standalone CI epic would carve one logical change into a work-type epic and leave each remediation epic's slice incomplete. |
| No onboarding chain | Rule 20 (not applicable) | Neither component is new: KServe is in the platform (architecture context `architecture/rhoai-3.0/kserve.md`, Konflux-onboarded) and Platform Operator is an established canonical RHAI component whose existing images the strategy remediates. No repo/konflux onboarding epics are generated; see Health Warnings for the Platform Operator context-file gap. |
| No Investigation epics | Step 3 decision rule | The strategy's open-questions table states "None on scope". The remaining unknowns (which images link which non-validated crypto libraries, and how to remediate each) do not change which epics exist or what they do — remediation proceeds the same way regardless, and a failed attempt is fix-and-retry. They are captured as scope/ACs on the remediation epics (module inventory per image is part of each epic's deliverable). Lab scheduling and review-board cadence are externally controlled schedule constraints, not unknowns. |

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic(s) | Notes |
|-----|----------|---------|-------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | RHAISTRAT-9013-E001, RHAISTRAT-9013-E002 | "All serving-stack images" splits along the component boundary (Rule 1): KServe's own images (including its serving data plane) in E001, the Platform Operator image(s) in E002. Both epics are P0 directly and as prerequisite epics of the P0 evidence epic. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | RHAISTRAT-9013-E003 | Evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results), submission through the security review board to the external certification lab. A distinct work stream (compliance artifact assembly vs. code remediation) with different review criteria, so it is its own epic rather than ACs on the remediation epics. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9013-E001 (bundled), RHAISTRAT-9013-E002 (bundled) | Bundled, not split: the CI FIPS-regression check is an enforcement deliverable over the exact same surfaces (serving-stack builds) that E001/E002 convert — it shares the builds, pipelines, and module-inventory data with the P0 remediation and could not ship as an independent epic with user value (a check over unconverted builds fails by definition). Per the shared-surface enforcement rule each surface epic authors and verifies the check's coverage for its own component's builds; a standalone epic would fragment one logical change and force a second pass over the same build configurations. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | RHAISTRAT-9013-E004 | Substantive new documentation topics (FIPS support posture, cluster prerequisites), a distinct work-product stream → separate `docs-authoring` epic. Priority P0 via the docs-authoring exception (strategy `priority: Critical`), not via inheritance. |

All four HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Health Warnings

1. **Missing strategy sections** (non-blocking): the strategy has no Impacted
   Teams table, no Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then acceptance criteria,
   and no Non-Functional Requirements section; Affected Components is a bare
   list with no change/owner detail. Decomposition proceeded from the
   available information.
2. **Team assignments are assumptions**: only KServe's owner (RHOAI Serving)
   is grounded, in `architecture/rhoai-3.0/kserve.md`. The Platform Operator
   epic is assigned to a placeholder owning team ("RHOAI Platform"), and the
   evidence/documentation epics to the serving-stack owner — confirm with the
   engagement before scheduling. In particular, the evidence epic is
   attributed to component KServe / team RHOAI Serving although its scope
   spans the Platform Operator images as well (it assembles evidence for the
   whole serving stack); the owning component/team for this cross-component
   evidence package must be confirmed before scheduling (also recorded on the
   epic's Risks/Notes).
3. **"Serving data plane" scope ambiguity**: the problem statement says
   "KServe components and the serving data plane" link non-validated crypto,
   but Affected Components lists only KServe and Platform Operator. Per the
   KServe architecture context, model execution in the data plane is provided
   by Serving Runtimes (vLLM, OpenVINO, Caikit). If the non-validated crypto
   lives in those runtime images, the strategy may be under-scoped — a
   follow-up strategy or scope amendment would be needed. Flagged for human
   verification.
4. **Platform Operator has no architecture-context file**: it is treated as
   in-platform because it appears in the canonical RHAI component list and the
   strategy premise is remediation of its existing images (not provisioning).
   No onboarding chain was generated. Signal 9 (architecture_claims) is
   scored 0 for its epic for this reason; verify its repository and pipeline
   status before starting.
5. **External schedule gates are risks, not ACs**: the accredited-lab
   turnaround (historically six to nine months) and security-review-board
   cadence are externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering
   effort. They are recorded as risks on the evidence epic; its ACs stop at
   the engineering completion point (evidence package assembled and submitted
   through the review board to the lab, accepted into review). The
   certification grant itself is outside epic scope.
6. **Bundled lower-priority HLR**: HLR-3 (P1) is bundled into the P0
   remediation epics per the shared-surface enforcement rule — rationale
   recorded in the HLR Traceability Matrix row above.

## Tiered Delivery

The external dependency with uncertain timing here is the certification
process itself (accredited lab, six-to-nine-month historical turnaround), not
an upstream code contribution — no upstream PR/RFC epic is generated (Rule 21
does not apply). Partial value is deliverable without the certification
outcome, so the decomposition tiers naturally:
